activities.title: Sink or Float
activities.description: Test which household objects sink or float in a bowl of water, guessing first.
activities.example: A rubber duck floated as guessed, but a metal spoon sinking surprised nobody -- until a hollow ball also sank!
materials: A bowl or sink of water
5-6 small household objects
steps: Gather a few small objects
Guess if each will sink or float
Drop it in and check

activities.title: Rainbow in a Jar
activities.description: Layer different-density liquids to make a colorful rainbow jar.
activities.example: The honey sank straight to the bottom while the oil floated clearly on top, with soapy water in between.
materials: A clear jar
Honey, dish soap, water, vegetable oil
Food coloring (optional)
steps: Pour honey in first, then dish soap
Slowly add colored water, then oil
Watch the layers separate by weight

activities.title: Shadow Hunt
activities.description: Go outside and trace or observe shadows at different times of day.
activities.example: Tracing the same tree's shadow at 10am and 2pm, they noticed it had moved and gotten shorter.
materials: Sidewalk chalk (optional)
steps: Find your shadow outside in the morning
Trace or mark where it falls
Check again later and compare

activities.title: Ice Melt Race
activities.description: Freeze two ice cubes and race to melt them using different methods.
activities.example: Salt melted the ice cube almost twice as fast as warm water did.
materials: Ice cubes
Salt, warm water, or sunlight to test
steps: Freeze a few ice cubes ahead of time
Try melting each one a different way
See which method wins the race

activities.title: Bubble Science
activities.description: Mix a simple bubble solution and experiment with different-shaped wands.
activities.example: A wand bent into a square still blew round bubbles every time -- a fun surprise.
materials: Dish soap, water, a bit of sugar
Pipe cleaners or straws for wands
steps: Mix dish soap, water, and a pinch of sugar
Bend a pipe cleaner into different shapes
Blow bubbles and see what shape they come out

activities.title: Baking Soda Volcano
activities.description: Build a mini volcano and trigger a baking-soda-and-vinegar eruption.
activities.example: Adding red food coloring made the eruption look like real lava, much to everyone's delight.
materials: Baking soda, vinegar, dish soap
A small container, clay or play-dough to shape a volcano
steps: Shape a mini volcano around a small container
Add baking soda, dish soap, and food coloring inside
Pour in vinegar and watch it erupt

activities.title: Paper Airplane Lab
activities.description: Build 3 different paper airplane designs and test which flies farthest.
activities.example: The simplest dart design flew farther than the fancy one with folded wings.
materials: Paper
A tape measure or long string
steps: Fold 3 different airplane designs
Launch each one the same way
Measure and compare how far each flew

activities.title: Magnet Hunt
activities.description: Use a magnet to search the house for which objects are magnetic and which aren't.
activities.example: Fridge magnets stuck to a metal spoon but not to an aluminum can -- a surprising discovery.
materials: A magnet
steps: Walk around with a magnet
Test different objects
Make two piles: magnetic and not

activities.title: Egg Drop Challenge
activities.description: Build a tiny cushioned container to protect an egg dropped from a height.
activities.example: A cotton-ball-padded cup survived a drop from the stairs, but round two from the balcony cracked it.
materials: A raw egg
Cushioning materials -- cotton, bubble wrap, cups
steps: Build a protective container for an egg
Drop it from a safe height outside
Check if it survived and try to improve the design

activities.title: Plant a Seed
activities.description: Plant a seed together and track its growth over the next few weeks.
activities.example: By day 9, the bean sprout had pushed its first tiny leaves through the soil.
materials: A seed (bean seeds sprout fast)
Soil, a small pot or cup
activities.duration: 15 min to plant, then daily check-ins
steps: Plant a seed in soil
Water it and place it somewhere sunny
Check on it every day and track its growth

activities.title: Build a Catapult
activities.description: Build a simple catapult from craft sticks and rubber bands, then test distance.
activities.example: After adjusting the rubber band tension, their mini marshmallow flew nearly 6 feet.
materials: Craft sticks, rubber bands, a plastic spoon
Small soft objects to launch (marshmallows, pom-poms)
steps: Build a small catapult from sticks and rubber bands
Launch a soft object and measure the distance
Adjust the design and try to beat your record

activities.title: Code a Simple Animation
activities.description: Use a free kid-friendly coding tool to make a character move.
activities.example: It took a few tries, but they got their cat character to walk across the screen and meow.
materials: A computer or tablet with internet access
steps: Open a beginner coding tool together
Pick a character and make it move
Add a sound or a second action

activities.title: Static Electricity Experiment
activities.description: Use a balloon to pick up small paper bits and talk about why it works.
activities.example: After rubbing the balloon on a sweater, it picked up tiny paper bits from across the table.
materials: A balloon
Small torn bits of tissue paper
steps: Rub a balloon on hair or fabric
Hold it near small paper bits
Talk about why the static charge pulls them

activities.title: Build a Circuit
activities.description: Use a simple battery-and-bulb kit to light up a small bulb.
activities.example: Connecting the wires the wrong way kept the bulb dark, until they flipped the battery around.
materials: A battery, a small bulb, wires (or a basic electronics kit)
steps: Connect a battery to a small bulb with wires
Troubleshoot if it doesn't light up right away
Try adding a switch if you have one

activities.title: Weather Tracker
activities.description: Track and chart the weather each day for a week, looking for patterns.
activities.example: By Friday, they noticed the temperature had dropped every single day that week.
materials: Paper or a notebook
steps: Check the weather each day at the same time
Record temperature and conditions
Look back at the end of the week for patterns

activities.title: DIY Water Filter
activities.description: Build a simple layered water filter from sand, gravel, and cloth, and test it on dirty water.
activities.example: The filtered water came out noticeably clearer than the muddy water they started with.
materials: A plastic bottle, sand, gravel, cloth or cotton
A cup of deliberately dirtied water
steps: Layer cloth, sand, and gravel in a cut bottle
Pour dirty water through it slowly
Compare the before and after

activities.title: Build a Simple App Idea
activities.description: Sketch out on paper how a simple app would work -- screens, buttons, and flow.
activities.example: Their homework-reminder app idea had just 3 screens, but they mapped out exactly how each button worked.
materials: Paper, pencil
steps: Pick a simple problem an app could solve
Sketch each screen it would need
Draw arrows showing how buttons connect the screens

activities.title: Chemical Reaction Lab
activities.description: Try a safe kitchen-chemistry reaction and explain the science.
activities.example: The "elephant toothpaste" reaction foamed up so fast it nearly overflowed the tray.
materials: Hydrogen peroxide, dish soap, yeast (for elephant toothpaste) -- or any safe kitchen reaction
steps: Pick a safe reaction to try (research it together first)
Set up the materials somewhere easy to clean
Try it and talk through what's chemically happening

activities.title: Energy Audit
activities.description: Walk through the house together finding ways to save energy, and estimate the impact.
activities.example: Switching 5 old bulbs to LEDs was the single biggest change they found.
materials: A notepad
steps: Walk through each room looking for energy waste
List ways to reduce it
Pick one change to actually make this week

activities.title: Build a Simple Robot
activities.description: Use a beginner robotics kit, or just design one on paper, together.
activities.example: Their paper-designed "robot" had a claw arm, solar panel, and a surprisingly detailed wiring diagram.
materials: A beginner robotics kit, or just paper and pencil
steps: Decide what the robot should do
Build it with a kit, or sketch and label the design on paper
Explain how each part would work
